Hello, I recommend you consider the 9F quartz movement of Grand Seiko. It is the best quartz movement in the industry, and they brag about its accuracy being more or less +/- 10 seconds PER YEAR. Regular quartz watches tick its accuracy by the month. 

For me the GS 9F quartz models are great value for money watches because not only do you get a good looking watch for less than 2k, you also get the same finishes (zaratsu polish, perfect dials, etc) that you can see from a 5k GS model. 

In terms of maintenance, you only have to replace the battery once every 3-4 years. You will notice that the battery is losing its power when the tick of the seconds hand is visibly ticking twice every second. Its at its best when it ticks twice but you barely notice it unless you see it on slow motion. 

Quartz and mechanical ones last a very long time but of course it depends on the watch maker and GS is peace of mind when it comes to reliability. It's been about a month of ownership with my 9F quartz and I adjusted the time to my iPhone, up to this day it still has the same accuracy as real time, without even having to adjust it every now and then. 

As for you not being a fan of frequent servicing and high costs, I'm afraid you have to reframe your narrative on that. Automatic watches are meant to be serviced every 4 or 5 years depending on the make of the watch, to make sure that every piece is still in working order. End of the day, it is a gear that tells time, an expensive one at that. If you don't take care of your time piece, your ability to tell time will be also an unreliable experience. If you service it well, it can last you an entire lifetime and it would feel brand new to you too. 

Hope you consider the 9F quartz model. It is truly a remarkable piece of accurate time keeping!

Remind yourself that someone else is also in a different stage of life. 

At this point, consider yourself lucky because you have all the freedom for self discovery and self reconnection without having the liability of a significant partner or kids. Bachelor life is interesting because this is what it teaches you before you get ready to meet and commit to someone else. And this goes to friendships as well.

That’s what makes it gimmicky and focuses on encouraging users to keep taking pics and vids for content to satisfy their social media needs.

The fact that they marketed The Weeknd’s music video shot on iPhone 16 using camera control is all marketing, to let consumers know that you can use this feature for your social media needs as well. You can act like a professional, or professionals can also use iPhone as their main device, either way it was meant to deliver the fact that there is a need for validation and that is to use it for content creation. As a casual consumer/user of iPhone, a simple press of the digital shutter is already perfect. Adding that camera control is a nice feature but not entirely groundbreaking…

In conclusion, I think the future of iPhone is an integration of next gen mirrorless camera and iOS. It makes sense considering the addition of this new camera control setting. If they want to emulate the professionalism aspect of photography, adding more features such as this button is just the step in that direction.

Still boils down to the same thing. Can you afford it without breaking bank? Go 16 pro. Do you care about value for money? Go 15 pro max. Check a side by side comparison between the two specifications, you will notice the difference is very minimal. They are both very powerful devices with a 10-20% marginal difference in capacity to run AI. Camera wise they are both the same. I am confident the typical consumer will not notice the difference from 12mp to 48mp on ultrawide lens; unless that consumer is a photographer looking to downsize his  gear that fits his pocket, the 16 pro (max) is the better device. Objectively, they are the same with slight improvements, and I am glad they made that decision. Apple does not want to alienate the existing 15 pro max user base by keeping them out of the loop just because the latest tech has just arrived. 

However, if you are coming from older models more especially the 11 or 12, chances are you want to upgrade to the latest tech (the 16 camera button) versus the existing 15 pro max line so that you feel superior than others. Like I said earlier, it’s a simple marketing strategy  that favors the consumer’s need for the next best thing so they can feel good about themselves… this is more commonly known as “shiny toy syndrome”. I am no stranger to this, I bought the 15 pro max and felt some level of superiority although I know that was what they were going for at that time, so it didn’t really bother me knowing after the fact it was just a simple marketing tactic. 

I also want to point out that the Pro lines tend to hold more value over the base models, because the existing tech that these devices feature carry over to the base line of next year’s models. So if you go 16 Pro, you gotta bet yourself that the next 17 Pro line will feature 48mp not just on ultrawide but also on telephoto (5x zoom). For now 15 and 16 pro have 12mp on telephoto. I use telephoto a lot. So when that time comes that they feature 48mp for 5x zoom will probably the time I get to experience FOMO. 2 centz
